nodes.description: Homozygous or compound heterozygous truncating CAST variants (frameshift, nonsense, splice-site, and one large deletion) abolish calpastatin. Patient cells show reduced CAST transcript through nonsense-mediated decay, reduced protein, and reduced calpastatin inhibitory activity.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutations in CAST cause peeling skin, leukonychia, acral punctate keratoses, cheilitis, and knuckle pads.
evidence.snippet: we identified homozygous mutations (c.607dup, c.424A>T, and c.1750delG) in CAST, all of which were predicted to encode truncated proteins

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutations in CAST cause peeling skin, leukonychia, acral punctate keratoses, cheilitis, and knuckle pads.
evidence.snippet: Immunohistochemistry shows that staining of calpastatin is reduced in skin from affected individuals.

evidence.reference_title: A novel homozygous nonsense mutation in CAST associated with PLACK syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Real-time qRT-PCR and immunoblot analysis showed reduced calpastatin expression in skin fibroblasts derived from both affected individuals compared to heterozygous family members. In vitro calpastatin activity assays also showed decreased activity in affected individuals.

evidence.reference_title: A patient with PLACK syndrome with a novel splicing mutation in CAST: the evidence for a loss-of-function mechanism through mis-splicing.
evidence.snippet: Segregation and expression analysis revealed that this loss-of-function via mRNA nonsense-mediated decay could be the causative pathogenic mechanism responsible for this patient's phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutations in CAST cause peeling skin, leukonychia, acral punctate keratoses, cheilitis, and knuckle pads.
evidence.snippet: loss-of-function mutations in calpastatin (CAST) are the genetic causes of an autosomal-recessive condition characterized by generalized peeling skin, leukonychia, acral punctate keratoses, cheilitis, and knuckle pads

evidence.reference_title: Peeling Skin, Leukonychia, Acral Punctate Keratoses, Cheilitis and Knuckle Pads (PLACK) Syndrome: An Updated Review of Cases and Identification of a Recurrent CAST Variant in Two Patients.
evidence.snippet: We describe two pediatric PLACK cases with a homozygous loss-of-function CAST variant (c.571G>T, p.Gly191Ter) which represents the only recurrent genetic variant of PLACK syndrome reported in the literature.

nodes.description: Proposed mechanism for the dilated cardiomyopathy seen in several PLACK families: calpastatin loss raises calpain activity in cardiomyocytes, degrading cytoskeletal and sarcomeric proteins and causing cardiomyocyte loss and fibrosis. Transgenic mice with cardiomyocyte-restricted calpain-1 or calpain-2 overexpression develop dilated cardiomyopathy. No patient myocardium has been examined for calpain activity, and the explanted-heart histology reported so far (hypertrophied cardiomyocytes, bizarre nuclei, fibrosis) is nonspecific.

evidence.reference_title: Leukonychia and peeling skin in an 11-year-old girl.
evidence.snippet: Excessive calpain activity may also lead to the degradation of key cytoskeletal proteins such as desmin and titin in myocardial fibers, leading to myocardial fibrosis and impaired contractility.

evidence.reference_title: Increased calpain-1 in mitochondria induces dilated heart failure in mice: role of mitochondrial superoxide anion.
evidence.snippet: Transgenic up-regulation of mitochondria-targeted CAPN1 dose-dependently induced cardiac cell death, adverse myocardial remodeling, heart failure, and early death in mice

nodes.description: Childhood-onset dilated cardiomyopathy (onset 4 to 15 years) in 7 of 27 reported patients, progressing to heart failure; three died, three received heart transplants and one needed a biventricular assist device. Penetrance appears incomplete and possibly age-dependent: affected siblings with the skin phenotype and normal echocardiograms have been reported, and no genotype-phenotype correlation for cardiac involvement has been found. One further patient's cardiomyopathy is attributed to a separate MYBPC3 variant.

evidence.reference_title: Leukonychia and peeling skin in an 11-year-old girl.
evidence.snippet: To date, there are 27 patients with PLACK syndrome reported, including ours, with 7 patients developed DCM. Among these, 3 had heart transplantation, 1 required a biventricular assist device, and 3 succumbed to progressive heart failure. The reported age of onset of DCM ranged from 4 to 15 years.

evidence.reference_title: Severe Dilated Cardiomyopathy with PLACK Syndrome Caused by a Novel Truncating Variant in the CAST Gene.
evidence.snippet: All affected children exhibited typical dermatological features of PLACK syndrome. Four developed severe DCM, two of whom required orthotopic heart transplantation.

evidence.reference_title: Severe Dilated Cardiomyopathy with PLACK Syndrome Caused by a Novel Truncating Variant in the CAST Gene.
evidence.snippet: No other variants in the genes known to cause cardiomyopathy were found.

evidence.reference_title: CASTing the net wider: A case report of PLACK syndrome associated with dilated cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: This case report highlights a case of PLACK syndrome presenting with the unique findings of striate hyperkeratosis on the palms as well as life-threatening cardiomyopathy.

evidence.reference_title: Concomitant PLACK Syndrome, MYBPC3-Related Cardiomyopathy, and Nutritional Deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Although the patient's cardiomyopathy is attributable to her MYBPC3 variant, this case adds to the growing list of reports describing PLACK syndrome with coinciding cardiomyopathy

nodes.description: Lesional skin shows widened intercellular spaces in the upper stratum spinosum, and CAST knockdown in cultured keratinocytes impairs their adhesion. Loss of cohesion between suprabasal keratinocytes is the structural basis of the superficial peeling.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutations in CAST cause peeling skin, leukonychia, acral punctate keratoses, cheilitis, and knuckle pads.
evidence.snippet: Transmission electron microscopy revealed widening of intercellular spaces with chromatin condensation and margination in the upper stratum spinosum in lesional skin, suggesting impaired intercellular adhesion as well as keratinocyte apoptosis.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutations in CAST cause peeling skin, leukonychia, acral punctate keratoses, cheilitis, and knuckle pads.
evidence.snippet: In vitro studies utilizing siRNA-mediated CAST knockdown revealed a role for calpastatin in keratinocyte adhesion.

evidence.reference_title: Peeling skin-leukonychia-acral punctate keratoses-cheilitis-knuckle pads syndrome
evidence.snippet: Histopathologic examination of affected skin areas is not specific and shows hyperkeratosis, acanthosis, and occasional intraepidermal clefting with irregular acantholysis.

nodes.description: TUNEL staining shows a significant increase in apoptotic keratinocytes in lesional skin, and electron microscopy shows chromatin condensation and margination in the upper stratum spinosum.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutations in CAST cause peeling skin, leukonychia, acral punctate keratoses, cheilitis, and knuckle pads.
evidence.snippet: A significant increase of apoptotic keratinocytes was also observed in TUNEL assays.

nodes.description: Calpastatin is the specific endogenous inhibitor of calpain-1 and calpain-2, so its loss is expected to leave calcium-activated calpain proteolysis unchecked. Calpain activity has not been measured in patient tissue, and the calpain substrates whose cleavage disrupts adhesion are not known; this node is inferred from the known function of calpastatin.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutations in CAST cause peeling skin, leukonychia, acral punctate keratoses, cheilitis, and knuckle pads.
evidence.snippet: Calpastatin is an endogenous specific inhibitor of calpain, a calcium-dependent cysteine protease.
